title: Diljit Dosanjh Stars in Imtiaz Ali's Partition Love Story 'Main Vaapas Aaunga' — And the Trailer Is Everything
excerpt: A.R. Rahman reunites with Imtiaz Ali and Irshad Kamil for a 78-year love story spanning the 1947 Partition, starring Diljit, Naseeruddin Shah, Vedang Raina, and Sharvari
body:
## The Trailer That Stopped the Timeline

If your WhatsApp family group hasn't forwarded the *Main Vaapas Aaunga* trailer yet, check your WiFi — because everyone else's has. Imtiaz Ali, the filmmaker who turned "Jab We Met" into a personality type and "Rockstar" into an emotional support album, is back with what might be his most ambitious work yet: a Partition-era love story that spans 78 years, stars Diljit Dosanjh and Naseeruddin Shah, and features an A.R. Rahman soundtrack. If that sentence didn't make you feel something, you might want to check your pulse.

The trailer, which dropped this week, opens with the golden wheat fields of undivided Punjab before fracturing into the chaos of 1947. At its centre is a love story that begins before the border and refuses to end after it — the kind of premise that hits differently when your dadi still tears up describing a village she left as a child.

## Imtiaz Ali's Most Personal Film

"Main Vaapas Aaunga is a personal story of love and longing which remained in someone's heart for 78 years after the partition of the country," Ali said in a statement accompanying the trailer release. For a director whose entire filmography is essentially about people chasing feelings across geography — Geet on a train to Bhatinda, Jordan busking in Prague, Ved losing himself in Corsica — a Partition love story feels almost inevitable.

But the scale is new. This isn't a backpacking romance or a college love triangle. This is Imtiaz Ali doing historical epic, produced by Birla Studios and Applause Entertainment alongside his own Window Seat Films (with Mohit Choudhary and Shibasish Sarkar producing). The period detailing in the trailer — the haveli interiors, the refugee trains, the costumes that shift across decades — suggests a production ambition that matches the emotional one.

**Vedang Raina** and **Sharvari** appear to play the younger versions of the central couple, while **Diljit Dosanjh** and **Naseeruddin Shah** anchor the present-day timeline. It's a casting masterstroke: Vedang's raw intensity (remember his debut in *The Archies*?) paired with Sharvari's increasingly commanding screen presence, bookended by two of Indian cinema's most magnetic performers.

## The Rahman-Kamil-Imtiaz Trio Reunites

Let's talk about the elephant in the room — or rather, the maestro in the recording studio. **A.R. Rahman** scoring an Imtiaz Ali film with lyrics by **Irshad Kamil** is the holy trinity of Hindi film music. This is the combination that gave us "Kun Faya Kun," "Tum Ho" from *Rockstar*, and "Patakha Guddi" from *Highway*. The first song, "Kya Kamaal Hai," has already started circulating on Instagram reels, and early reactions suggest this soundtrack could be another classic.

For the global desi community, Rahman's involvement alone makes this an event film. The man's Oscar sits on mantlepieces in the imagination of every NRI kid who grew up watching the 2009 ceremony on a grainy stream.

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

Diljit Dosanjh is no longer just a Punjabi music star. After Coachella, after a global arena tour that sold out in minutes from Vancouver to Melbourne, after *Crew* and *Jatt & Juliet 3*, he has become the diaspora's favourite cultural export. Seeing him in an Imtiaz Ali period drama — speaking Punjabi, navigating Partition, opposite Naseeruddin Shah — is the kind of artistic leap that turns a star into a legend.

And Partition stories? They're not historical curiosities for NRI families. They're living memory. The grandparent who never went back. The village no one can find on Google Maps anymore. The recipe that crossed the border but the house that didn't. *Main Vaapas Aaunga* — "I will come back" — isn't just a film title. For millions in the diaspora, it's a sentence that echoes across generations.

https://www.instagram.com/diljitdosanjh/

Interestingly, Diljit has announced he'll skip traditional promotional rounds for the film, letting the work speak for itself — a move that feels very on-brand for a performer who once told an interviewer that "the music should be louder than the marketing."

## What's Next

*Main Vaapas Aaunga* releases on **June 12, 2026**. With the Rahman soundtrack likely to drop in stages over the coming weeks, expect your Spotify Discover Weekly to get significantly more emotional. For NRIs planning summer India trips, this might just be the film that finally gets the whole family — three generations, one multiplex, several tissue boxes — into the same theatre.

Mark your calendars. Better yet, mark your hearts.
